summary: Everything orbits Jev, a tiny cheap decision model, and Needle, a free offline rival. Plus the open-source repos of the week (OpenSEO, Paperclip, Orca, ECC, Agent Skills) and Claude Code adopting agents.md. Best for Charlie: agents.md support, Agent Skills, ECC.

tools.name: Jev
tools.what: Tiny, very fast decision model (not a chatbot) that answers multiple-choice and yes/no questions with probabilities, cheaply.
tools.shown: Sorted 500 emails live, built a voice-controlled browser, model routing, support triage, lead scoring, agent memory search, clip scoring and smart-home control.
tools.quote: It's not a chatbot. It can't even write a sentence.
tools.check: Pricing not stated; waitlist said to be gone and also available via OpenRouter; not for high-stakes predictions (trading) per the video.

opinion.why: Calls it worthwhile and wants it for sorting email and finding his own video clips.
opinion.quote: I think it's great and it's worthwhile.

our_view.for_what: Sorting a pile of comments or emails if the channel ever gets one
our_view.why: Charlie has no 500-email pile yet, so no real pain. Rule 39 (adopt tools only for real pain); Rule 42 (lowest rung first). Any API key goes in .env (Rule 26).

tools.name: Jev
tools.what: Fast decision model that lets you talk to a Mac app and have it act, cheaply.
tools.shown: Clip of someone speaking to the computer to open Notes and create a note; hosts did not try it.
tools.quote: Here's the thing about uh Jev, it now no longer has a waitlist.
tools.check: Mac app claim; pricing not stated.

opinion.why: Wants the talk-to-your-Mac demo for himself but says no download exists.
opinion.quote: this is something I would love to have.

our_view.why: A Mac-only app nobody has published, so nothing to adopt. Rule 39.

tools.name: Meta Muse
tools.what: Free consumer AI agent from Meta that people use to find cheaper insurance, cancel forgotten subscriptions and find money owed.
tools.shown: Walked through other people's examples and showed a simple chat screen; hosts did not run it themselves.
tools.quote: People are banking money with Muse, the free AI agent from Facebook.
tools.check: Savings claims ($3,500 cheaper insurance etc.) are social-media anecdotes, unverified.

opinion.why: Likes the savings stories but says any agent could do them.
opinion.quote: I think this is great. I don't think it's unique to Muse though.

our_view.why: Insurance, receipts and money owed are private finance, which never goes in this public repo. Rule 36 (read-only first) and Rule 39 (no pain, no tool).

tools.name: Clueso
tools.what: Turns a rough screen recording into a polished demo, training video or SOP with zooms and voiceover.
tools.shown: Played a launch demo video made with it.
tools.quote: this in my mind is like Screen Studio, but easier to use
tools.check: Pricing not stated; auto-caption spells it Cluso.

opinion.why: Sees it as an easier Screen Studio for polished demo, training or SOP videos.
opinion.quote: this in my mind is like Screen Studio, but easier to use

our_view.for_what: Polishing screen recordings of Claude Code builds for the channel
our_view.why: Fits the channel, but price is unknown. Rule 43 (measure on your own work first): try it on one real recording.

tools.name: NewsJack
tools.what: Free open-source agent skills that research journalists and stories and write pitches, like a PR team.
tools.shown: Showed Elvis's demo plugging Jev into it to scrape and pitch quickly and cheaply.
tools.quote: It's a free GitHub repo and these skills basically turn your agent into a PR team.
tools.check: Claimed 8-15k a month PR cost comparison not verified.

opinion.why: Calls it a cool skill suite, but nobody says they would use it.

our_view.why: Pitching journalists is a business job, not an AI OS or channel-building job yet. Rule 39.

tools.name: ChatGPT Voice
tools.what: ChatGPT voice mode now reaches email, calendar and Slack through connectors.
tools.shown: Played OpenAI's launch video; Andrew said the email part did not work until he updated the app.
tools.quote: connector access, it's going to make it a hundred times more useful.
tools.check: Which plan gets connectors not stated.

opinion.why: Wants voice mode to read and reply to email while driving.
opinion.quote: so looking forward to driving and then replying to email

our_view.why: Voice with email and calendar access is exactly the broad access Rule 36 says to start read-only; he also could not get it working. Rule 39.

tools.name: Sider Omni
tools.what: AI sidebar that sits on top of almost any app so you can ask about what is on screen.
tools.shown: Showed a demo with Apple Mail; The co-host said he would not use it.
tools.quote: It adds it to just about any app you have.
tools.check: Pricing not stated.

opinion.why: Says it is a habit tool and not his habit, though fine for people who already do it.
opinion.quote: this isn't a tool that I would necessarily find myself using

our_view.why: Claude Code already sits where Charlie works; a sidebar adds nothing. Rule 39.

tools.name: Camera Bench
tools.what: Free repo that has AI watch your webcam in real time and describe faces, gestures or custom yes/no checks.
tools.shown: Showed it reading expressions and finger counts live.
tools.quote: it's a free GitHub repo for AI to essentially watch your camera, right?
tools.check: Link list names the repo Glance Speedlab; URL taken from there.

opinion.why: A cool technical feat, but he struggled to find a real use for it.
opinion.quote: we were kind of struggling to come up with like an actual use case

our_view.why: A demo with no use. Rule 39 (adopt tools only for real pain).

tools.name: Claude Opus 5.5
tools.what: New Claude model praised for writing, visual design and animation.
tools.shown: Showed community examples including a music video animation and a walkable shop built with it.
tools.quote: it just is the best feeling model we've we've had in a long time.
tools.check: Opinion only; no benchmarks or pricing given.

opinion.why: Says it is the best-feeling model in a long time, best for writing and visual design.
opinion.quote: it just is the best feeling model we've we've had in a long time.

our_view.for_what: Scripts, titles and descriptions for the channel, and running the OS
our_view.why: Likely worth it, but it is a feeling, not a test. Rule 43 (same prompt, own work) and Rule 41 (prune after every new model); run the audit content check after switching.

tools.name: Systo Commerce
tools.what: Vibe-coded walkable online mall where you shop as an avatar and stores sell real goods and ad space.
tools.shown: Showed a demo clip of an avatar trying on a jacket.
tools.quote: you can walk into different stores
tools.check: Built with Claude Opus 5.5; demo only.

opinion.why: Calls it a cool demo, nothing about using it.

our_view.why: A demo mall, not a tool for Charlie. Rule 39.

tools.name: Needle
tools.what: Tiny free on-device LLM (8-29 MB) that turns plain requests into safe structured tool calls with confidence scores, offline.
tools.shown: Live demos: smart-home lights, reminders and note search, a robot vacuum, phone and laptop actions.
tools.quote: There's a free LLM that works like Jev, so it will make no mistakes.
tools.check: 'No mistakes' is a marketing line; the guest says reliability depends on tightly scoped tools and confidence scores. Title says better than Jev, not shown.

opinion.why: Tells software builders to put it in when they want a free LLM inside their own app.
opinion.quote: yes, you should absolutely put Needle in if what you want is this LLM that's self-contained and free and part of your software

our_view.why: Charlie is not shipping software with a model inside. The guest also says quality depends on how tools are scoped, so 'no mistakes' needs testing first (Rule 17).

tools.name: GrokBot
tools.what: Always-on agent used as the orchestrator that wires voice, phone, CRM and forms together.
tools.shown: Guest built an outbound sales-call system live from a voice-note plan, using it as the orchestrator.
tools.quote: I would think of Grok Bot as the as the orchestrator agent.
tools.check: Name per auto-captions and description; $16,000 booked revenue is the guest's claim.

opinion.why: Uses it daily and loves how quick and easy it is.
opinion.quote: I've been loving it. It's so easy, so quick

our_view.why: He admits other agents can do the same, and Charlie already has Claude Code and Codex. Rule 39; Rule 43 before switching.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what: Voice agent platform; here it runs the phone conversations, with the founder's cloned voice.
tools.shown: Set up the voice agent and cloned voice in the build.
tools.quote: you go ahead and add 11 Labs
tools.check: Pricing not stated.

opinion.why: The guest cloned his own voice so callers hear someone like them.
opinion.quote: They want somebody that talks like them and sounds like them when they get on the phone.

our_view.why: Phone sales is not Charlie's job. A cloned voice for videos is a later question, and Rule 37 says check before anything goes public.

tools.name: Twilio
tools.what: Provides the phone number the voice agent calls from.
tools.shown: Bought and registered a number live.
tools.quote: The telephone number from Twilio.
tools.check: Pricing not stated.

opinion.why: Says buying and registering the number was easy.
opinion.quote: It was nothing.

our_view.why: Only needed for phone calls. Paid and UK number rules apply. Rule 39.

tools.name: Open Code Review
tools.what: Alibaba's open-source code reviewer for vibe coders, now with a VS Code extension, using your existing AI subscription.
tools.shown: Hosts showed the repo and discussed running it on commit; not installed live.
tools.quote: Alibaba's code reviewer now leaves the terminal.
tools.check: Hosts say open-source versions let you use existing subscriptions instead of paid tools.

opinion.why: Likes open versions that let his firm use its existing subscriptions instead of paid reviewers.
opinion.quote: more and more of these open-source versions are coming out that just let us use our existing cloud subscriptions or tokens or whatever

our_view.why: Their firm ships code at scale; Charlie's checks are tools/audit.py and the audit skill. Rule 33 says a separate checker is wanted, and we have one.

tools.name: OpenSEO
tools.what: Open-source Semrush rival; self-host free or have it hosted for about 10 dollars a month.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and debate about its Y Combinator funding; Adam is a paying customer.
tools.quote: Semrush rival that you basically pay peanuts for
tools.check: Hosted price of 10 dollars a month is as spoken.

opinion.why: A paying customer who calls it a great tool and a wrapper he has no problem with.
opinion.quote: I think it's a great tool.

our_view.why: Web SEO tool; Charlie has no website, and YouTube search is covered by vidIQ. Rule 39.

tools.name: Paperclip
tools.what: Dashboard that organises many agents like a company so you can assign tasks and see who does what.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and a popular video about it; not run live.
tools.quote: allows you to manage your agents like their employees
tools.check: Works with OpenClaw and Hermes; pitched at more advanced agents.

opinion.why: Thinks an agent manager is useful but is not sure this is the right one.
opinion.quote: I think this is the kind of thing that's useful. I don't know if this is the right project for it

our_view.why: One person with a few agents does not need an org chart. Rule 24 (sub-agents not overused) and Rule 39 (cap parallel sessions).

tools.name: Anthropic Financial Services
tools.what: Anthropic's skill pack for finance work such as stock analysis and know-your-customer screening.
tools.shown: Discussed a user who analysed a stock with it; not run live.
tools.quote: financial company sitting there and analyzing stocks for you.
tools.check: Finance output should not be trusted blindly.

opinion.why: Says most listeners will not need it, then admits a lawyer gets real value from similar skills.
opinion.quote: most people who are listening are not going to need this

our_view.why: Finance and know-your-customer work is not Charlie's, and finance details stay out of this public repo. Rule 39.

tools.name: Claude Code agents.md support
tools.what: Claude Code now reads the shared agents.md instruction file, so one file serves Claude and Codex.
tools.shown: Explained why one shared instruction file ends the claude.md versus agents.md mismatch; no demo.
tools.quote: typically they're looking at an agents.md file that's in your project folder
tools.check: Skills are still not shared between Claude and Codex, per the hosts; check Claude Code docs for the exact behaviour.

opinion.why: Calls the shared instruction file a small win that ends the claude.md versus agents.md mess.
opinion.quote: the fact that they're going to use the same file that everyone else is using means that the mess just goes away.

our_view.for_what: Keep AGENTS.md as the one instruction file for Claude Code and Codex
our_view.why: Already how this OS works: CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md. Rule 3 (one current source per fact). Check the Claude Code docs before dropping the import, as the hosts do not demo it.

tools.name: ECC
tools.what: Huge skill pack with plan-to-verify loops and memory that improves your agent over time.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and the remember/improve features; compared it to Agent Skills.
tools.quote: You get all that experience baked into your cloud for free.
tools.check: Hosts call it a lot for a beginner; Agent Skills is easier to start.

opinion.why: Great for power users, overwhelming for a new user.
opinion.quote: If you're if you're a new user, it's a little overwhelming.

our_view.for_what: Borrow the remember-and-improve idea; install none of its 292 skills
our_view.why: Matches Rule 41 (smallest context) and Rule 34 (skills built from a real run). Rule 37: vet any plugin before installing, and ask on the Decision Desk.

tools.name: WeKnora
tools.what: Tencent's open-source knowledge system that links files into a searchable graph wiki for your agents.
tools.shown: Described and showed the repo; not installed live.
tools.quote: Obsidian plus rag plus a graph database plus some extra integrations
tools.check: Auto-caption mishears the name as Nora.

opinion.why: Likes that it links files and builds the structure for him; he never had the patience to do it by hand.
opinion.quote: you could just point this at your computer and all your files and it will build those relationships automatically.

our_view.why: Charlie's OS is organised by hand so he can find things without search (Rule 6) and raw sources stay untouched (Rule 12). Pointing it at all your files also breaks Rule 36 for a public repo.

tools.name: Agent Skills
tools.what: Addy Osmani's pack of workflow skills that stops agents taking shortcuts; easier to install than ECC.
tools.shown: Compared side by side with ECC using a Claude comparison.
tools.quote: So maybe agent skills is easier if you're just getting into this
tools.check: Hosts frame it as easier, not better; ECC has far more skills.

opinion.why: Recommends it over ECC for someone just getting into this.
opinion.quote: So maybe agent skills is easier if you're just getting into this

our_view.for_what: Read its 25 skills for ideas on spec, plan and review steps
our_view.why: Easier than ECC is fair. Rule 34 (one job, built from a real run) and Rule 37 (vet before install); install nothing without the Decision Desk.

tools.name: Knowledge Work Plugins
tools.what: Anthropic's plugins for finance, HR, legal, marketing and operations work.
tools.shown: Discussed browsing the marketing plugin to learn its structure; no live run.
tools.quote: This is for uh knowledge workers. It's a collection of skills like how to do finance, human resources, legal, marketing, operations.

opinion.why: Thinks the plugins are a good way for a non-expert to level up in areas like marketing.
opinion.quote: this is probably a great spot for for the everyman to level up

our_view.for_what: Read the marketing plugin to learn how a good plugin is built
our_view.why: Learning its structure is cheap and safe. Rule 37 (plugin vetting) before installing; check research/plugin-map.md first.

tools.name: Orca
tools.what: Interface for running several coding agents side by side, designed around agents rather than code.
tools.shown: Showed the readme screenshot with Claude Code and Codex in one window plus mobile link.
tools.quote: Run five coding agents at once. Keep the best.
tools.check: 77,000 stars claim as spoken; hosts say tools like this will replace traditional IDEs, an opinion.

opinion.why: Calls it awesome and a new kind of editor designed around agents, not code.
opinion.quote: I would call this the new era of VS Code

our_view.why: Several agents at once is the opposite of one next step at a time. Rule 24 and Rule 39 (cap parallel sessions).

tools.name: Octop
tools.what: Tencent Cloud's open-source team/family agent assistant, aimed at Asian chat apps.
tools.shown: Browsed the repo and its supported apps.
tools.quote: This is their opensource version of Grockbot
tools.check: Integrations target apps popular in Asia, not the UK.

opinion.why: Aimed at chat apps popular in Asia, not the West.
opinion.quote: right now this looks like it's targeted more for Asia

our_view.why: Telegram and QQ style apps; Charlie is in the UK and needs nothing like it. Rule 39.

tools.name: Claude Code Templates
tools.what: Browsable catalogue of Claude Code skills, plugins and commands.
tools.shown: Showed the marketplace-style site; about 900 skills and 34 plugins.
tools.quote: This is a collection of Claude Code add-ons.
tools.check: Counts are as spoken; check each add-on before installing.

opinion.why: Says it is worth a bookmark as a browsable place to find skills and plugins.
opinion.quote: this would be a a worthy of a bookmark

our_view.for_what: Browse for ideas, not for installing
our_view.why: Fine to browse. Being 'curated' is not vetting, so Rule 37 still applies before any install.

vs.gap: A catalogue you pick single skills from, where ECC is one big pack; we don't know which of its skills are worth adding for a beginner.
